newsitem.title: USA: Maine Republican senators back EPA air proposal.
newsitem.headline: Maine Republican senators back EPA air proposal.

text.p: Maine's two Republican senators have endorsed the Environmental Protection Agency's proposal to tighten air quality standards, bringing to three the number of Senate Republicans on record endorsing the plan.

"We stand ready to support the proposed revisions to air quality standards, and seek your assurance that these standards be accompanied by measures addressing the issue of polluted air that enters Maine from other states," Sens. Olympia Snowe and Susan Collins said in a letter sent late last week to President Clinton.
They said pollution drifting in from other states accounted for at least 60 percent of Maine's air pollution.

"It is crucial that no additional restrictions be applied to the state until control strategies are put in place to alleviate the air pollution at its sources outside the state," Snowe and Collins said in their letter to Clinton.
The administration is debating whether to impose stricter air standards endorsed by health advocates but opposed by industry.
